title: Textured, modelled geometry instead of flat-coloured cubes, in raylib
note: Load models and textures through studio::asset, mipmap them and tag every draw: a flat colour is a defect.
intent: A flat-coloured DrawCube is a placeholder, never the game. Load each model once in reset (studio::assetModel for GLB/glTF without Draco or OBJ, studio::asset for PNG/JPEG textures), give textures mipmaps and trilinear filtering so they hold up at distance, and draw through studio::drawModel or studio::drawModelEx after studio::tag("<thing>") so the runtime counts each draw under its name. Procedural detail is fine when it is textured: GenImageChecked, GenImagePerlinNoise or a gradient image turned into a mipmapped texture reads as a surface, a bare colour does not. A missing asset shows as a magenta checker, which is a visible bug to fix, not a crash.
port: Assets live under assets/ and are loaded only through studio::asset/assetModel/assetSound, which resolve the same path on every destination.

evidence.note: A flat colour with no texture is a defect: use textures and models from assets/ via studio::asset().
The starter itself draws a mipmapped procedural checker on a plane and a cube, tagged ground and block.
